claims.text: The alloy has the composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 in atomic percent.
The as-cast alloy solidifies through a complex, multistep crystallization sequence.
Several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases form during solidification.
Rapid quenching can bypass high-temperature nucleation in this alloy.
The proposed intervention is a short isothermal hold at Tg + 10–20 °C after rapid quenching and before final cooling.
The proposed hold should last from seconds to a few minutes.
A hold just above Tg permits stress and structural relaxation in the undercooled liquid.
The near-Tg hold promotes chemical homogenization and minimizes compositional inhomogeneities.
The near-Tg hold reduces local free-volume fluctuations and internal stresses.
Reduced free-volume and compositional fluctuations decrease the number of nucleation sites for primary crystallization.
A sufficiently brief near-Tg hold can produce relaxation without triggering extensive nucleation.
The resulting relaxed amorphous matrix has a higher activation barrier for crystallization during reheating.
Relative to continuous rapid cooling, the intervention will increase the retained amorphous-phase fraction.
Relative to continuous rapid cooling, the intervention will increase the DSC crystallization-onset temperature.
Relative to continuous rapid cooling, the intervention will reduce the intensity of crystallization exotherms during reheating.
Continuous rapid quenching without the intermediate hold leads to extensive primary crystallization.
Continuously quenched material exhibits multiple exothermic signals during reheating.
The cooling rate must be sufficiently high to bypass extensive nucleation.
Hold temperatures or durations outside a narrow near-Tg, short-duration window may induce nucleation or eliminate the anticipated benefit.
The optimal hold temperature, hold duration, and bulk uniformity of the effect are not established for this alloy.

contradictions.description: Rapid quenching is described as avoiding or bypassing extensive primary nucleation, while the stated continuous-rapid-quench baseline is said to produce extensive primary crystallization. The distinction between merely reducing crystallization and actually bypassing it is not resolved.
